questions.topic: De Broglie wavelength of a slow neutron
questions.learningObjective: Compute neutron de Broglie wavelength at thermal energy
questions.stem: A translator's note gives a neutron kinetic energy of 0.025 eV; find its de Broglie wavelength in nm.
questions.explanation: Neutron mass is about 1.675e-27 kg. Using lambda equals h over sqrt of 2 m K with K equals 0.025 eV gives about 0.181 nm, comparable to atomic spacing.
questions.hint: Use neutron mass in p equals sqrt of 2 m K.

questions.topic: The two usable forms of the de Broglie relation
questions.learningObjective: Identify the two forms of de Broglie relation
questions.stem: A translator asks which two expressions both give the de Broglie wavelength of a particle.

options.text: lambda equals h over p and lambda equals h over sqrt of 2 m K.
lambda equals h over p and lambda equals h over m v.
lambda equals h f and lambda equals c over f.
lambda equals h over m v and lambda equals c over f.

questions.explanation: The de Broglie relation lambda equals h over p can be written using p equals m v or p equals sqrt of 2 m K for nonrelativistic particles. Both forms are valid.
questions.hint: Express momentum in two ways.

questions.topic: Momentum of a particle from its de Broglie wavelength
questions.stem: A particle has de Broglie wavelength 0.10 nm; what is its momentum?

options.text: About 6.63e-15 kg m/s, using eV instead of meters.
About 6.63e-34 kg m/s, using h without dividing.
About 6.63e-24 kg m/s, from h over lambda.
About 6.63e-43 kg m/s, dividing by h instead.

questions.explanation: Momentum p equals h over lambda. With h equals 6.626e-34 J s and lambda equals 0.10e-9 m, p is about 6.63e-24 kg m/s.
questions.hint: Use p equals h over lambda.

questions.topic: Why an electron microscope resolves more than a light microscope
questions.learningObjective: Explain resolution advantage of electron microscopes
questions.stem: A note compares electron wavelength 0.01 nm with visible light 500 nm; which microscope resolves smaller features?

options.text: Neither resolves features smaller than 1 nm.
The light microscope, because longer wavelength carries more energy.
They resolve the same features because both use waves.
The electron microscope, because its shorter wavelength gives better resolution.

questions.explanation: Resolution is limited by wavelength; shorter wavelength means smaller resolvable features. Electron wavelengths are thousands of times shorter than visible light.
questions.hint: Shorter wavelength means better resolution.

questions.topic: De Broglie wavelength at a higher accelerating voltage
questions.stem: A diagram shows electron wavelength decreasing as accelerating voltage increases; explain why.

options.text: Higher voltage increases photon energy, shortening wavelength.
Higher voltage gives higher kinetic energy and momentum, shortening wavelength.
Higher voltage decreases mass, shortening wavelength.
Higher voltage reduces Planck's constant, shortening wavelength.

questions.explanation: Accelerating voltage increases kinetic energy, which increases momentum. Since lambda equals h over p, higher momentum means shorter wavelength.
questions.hint: Voltage to energy to momentum to wavelength.

questions.topic: De Broglie wavelength of a macroscopic object
questions.learningObjective: Estimate wavelength of a macroscopic object
questions.stem: A note computes the de Broglie wavelength of a 0.1 kg ball moving at 10 m/s and gets 6.6e-34 m; check.

options.text: Wrong, macroscopic objects have no wavelength.
Wrong, it should use photon energy instead.
Correct, lambda equals h over m v equals 6.6e-34 m.
Wrong, mass should be in eV not kg.

questions.explanation: lambda equals h over m v equals 6.626e-34 divided by (0.1 times 10) equals 6.626e-34 m. The tiny wavelength explains why wave effects are unobservable for macroscopic objects.
questions.hint: Use lambda equals h over m v.

questions.topic: Why neutrons diffract from crystal planes
questions.stem: Explain why thermal neutrons diffract from crystal planes.

answer.exemplar: Thermal neutrons have kinetic energy about 0.025 eV, giving de Broglie wavelength near 0.18 nm. This matches typical crystal plane spacings, so Bragg diffraction occurs just as with X-rays.

questions.explanation: Neutron wavelength matches interatomic spacing, satisfying the Bragg condition. This is why crystals diffract neutrons.
questions.hint: Match neutron wavelength to lattice spacing.

questions.topic: Energy of the third energy level of hydrogen
questions.stem: Find the energy of the n equals 3 level of hydrogen in eV.
questions.explanation: E n equals negative 13.6 over n squared eV. For n equals 3, E 3 equals negative 13.6 over 9, about negative 1.51 eV.
questions.hint: Use E n equals -13.6 over n squared.

questions.topic: Energy needed to excite hydrogen from the ground state to n equal to 3
questions.stem: Find the energy in eV needed to excite hydrogen from n equals 1 to n equals 3.
questions.explanation: E 1 is negative 13.6 eV and E 3 is negative 1.51 eV. The difference is 12.09 eV.
questions.hint: Subtract E 1 from E 3.

questions.topic: Wavelength emitted in the drop from n equal to 2 to n equal to 1
questions.stem: Hydrogen drops from n equals 2 to n equals 1; what wavelength is emitted?

options.text: About 1875 nm, from inverting the energy.
About 656.3 nm, from the n equals 3 to n equals 2 transition.
About 102.6 nm, from adding level energies.
About 121.6 nm, from 10.2 eV photon energy.

questions.explanation: Energy difference is 13.6 times (1 minus 1/4) equals 10.2 eV. Wavelength equals 1240 over 10.2, about 121.6 nm.
questions.hint: Use delta E equals 1240 over lambda.

questions.topic: De Broglie wavelength of a slow neutron
questions.stem: A neutron moves at 2000 m/s; what is its de Broglie wavelength?

options.text: About 0.000199 nm, dividing by 1000.
About 0.199 nm, from h over m v.
About 199 nm, multiplying by 1000.
About 6.63e-34 nm, using h alone.

questions.explanation: lambda equals h over m v equals 6.626e-34 divided by (1.675e-27 times 2000), about 1.98e-10 m or 0.199 nm.
questions.hint: Use lambda equals h over m v.

questions.topic: The two usable forms of the de Broglie relation
questions.learningObjective: Choose correct form for a given quantity
questions.stem: A note has kinetic energy K but not speed; which form should be used?

options.text: lambda equals h f, using photon energy.
lambda equals h over m v, but v must be guessed.
lambda equals h over sqrt of 2 m K.
lambda equals c over f, using light speed.

questions.explanation: When kinetic energy is known, use p equals sqrt of 2 m K, so lambda equals h over sqrt of 2 m K. No separate speed is needed.
questions.hint: Pick the form that uses known K.

questions.topic: Momentum of a particle from its de Broglie wavelength
questions.learningObjective: Compute momentum from wavelength in nm
questions.stem: A diagram shows wavelength 0.05 nm; find momentum in kg m/s.

options.text: About 6.63e-24 kg m/s, using 0.1 nm instead.
About 1.33e-26 kg m/s, using nm without conversion.
options.misconception: uses nm without converting to meters

options.text: About 3.31e-24 kg m/s, dividing h by 2.
About 1.33e-23 kg m/s, from h over 0.05e-9 m.

questions.explanation: p equals h over lambda equals 6.626e-34 divided by 0.05e-9, about 1.33e-23 kg m/s.
questions.hint: Convert nm to m first.

questions.topic: Why an electron microscope resolves more than a light microscope
questions.stem: A note claims light microscopes can resolve atoms because lenses are high quality; find the error.

options.text: Lens quality does determine resolution, so the note is correct.
Resolution is limited by wavelength, not lens quality alone.
Atoms are too small for any microscope to resolve.
Light wavelength can be shortened arbitrarily with filters.

questions.explanation: Even perfect lenses cannot resolve features much smaller than the wavelength used. Visible light wavelengths are hundreds of nanometers, far larger than atoms.
questions.hint: Resolution limit comes from wavelength.

questions.topic: De Broglie wavelength at a higher accelerating voltage
questions.learningObjective: Compute wavelength at a new voltage
questions.stem: Explain how doubling the accelerating voltage changes an electron's de Broglie wavelength.

answer.exemplar: Doubling the voltage doubles the kinetic energy. Since momentum grows as the square root of energy, momentum increases by sqrt of 2. Wavelength decreases by the same factor, becoming about 0.707 of its original value.

questions.explanation: Voltage to energy to momentum to wavelength. Doubling energy multiplies momentum by sqrt of 2 and divides wavelength by sqrt of 2.
questions.hint: Track energy, momentum, then wavelength.

questions.topic: De Broglie wavelength of a macroscopic object
questions.learningObjective: Compute wavelength of a slow macroscopic object
questions.stem: Find the de Broglie wavelength in meters of a 1 kg object moving at 1 m/s.
questions.explanation: lambda equals h over m v equals 6.626e-34 divided by (1 times 1), about 6.63e-34 m. The wavelength is astronomically small.
questions.hint: Use lambda equals h over m v.

questions.topic: Why neutrons diffract from crystal planes
questions.learningObjective: Select the condition for neutron diffraction
questions.stem: If neutron wavelength is 0.18 nm and plane spacing is 0.18 nm, how many wavelengths fit across one spacing at normal incidence?
questions.explanation: At normal incidence the path difference is 2 d sin theta. For first-order diffraction with theta about 30 degrees, one wavelength fits across the round trip. The simple count at normal incidence is one wavelength per spacing.
questions.hint: Think of one wavelength per plane spacing.

questions.topic: Energy of the third energy level of hydrogen
questions.stem: What is the energy of the n equals 4 level of hydrogen?

options.text: About -1.51 eV, from -13.6 over 9.
About -3.40 eV, from -13.6 over 4.
About -0.85 eV, from -13.6 over 16.
About -13.6 eV, from -13.6 over 1.

questions.explanation: E n equals negative 13.6 over n squared. For n equals 4, E equals negative 13.6 over 16, about negative 0.85 eV.
questions.hint: Square n in the denominator.

questions.topic: Energy needed to excite hydrogen from the ground state to n equal to 3
questions.stem: What wavelength photon is needed to excite hydrogen from n equals 1 to n equals 3?

options.text: About 1875 nm, from inverting the energy.
About 121.6 nm, from the n equals 2 to n equals 1 energy.
About 656.3 nm, from the n equals 3 to n equals 2 transition.
About 102.6 nm, from 1240 over 12.09 eV.

questions.explanation: Excitation energy is 12.09 eV. Wavelength equals 1240 divided by 12.09, about 102.6 nm.
questions.hint: Use lambda equals 1240 over delta E.

questions.topic: Wavelength emitted in the drop from n equal to 2 to n equal to 1
questions.stem: The n equals 2 to n equals 1 transition belongs to which series?

options.text: The Balmer series, visible light.
The Lyman series, ultraviolet.
The Paschen series, infrared.
The Brackett series, far infrared.

questions.explanation: Transitions ending at n equals 1 form the Lyman series, in the ultraviolet. The n equals 2 to 1 line is Lyman alpha at 121.6 nm.
questions.hint: Series are named by final level.

questions.topic: De Broglie wavelength of a slow neutron
questions.stem: A diagram compares a 0.025 eV neutron with a 100 eV electron; which wavelength is longer?

options.text: They are equal because both are matter waves.
The electron wavelength is longer because electron mass is smaller.
The neutron wavelength is longer despite lower energy, due to its mass.
Neither has a wavelength because only photons do.

questions.explanation: Neutron wavelength at 0.025 eV is about 0.18 nm, while electron at 100 eV is 0.123 nm. The neutron's much lower energy gives it a longer wavelength despite larger mass.
questions.hint: Compute both wavelengths.

questions.topic: The two usable forms of the de Broglie relation
questions.learningObjective: Derive one form from the other
questions.stem: A note writes lambda equals h over m v and also lambda equals h over sqrt of 2 m K, claiming they always differ; find the error.

options.text: They are equivalent only for photons.
They always differ because mass appears differently.
They differ unless velocity is zero.
They are equivalent when K equals one half m v squared.

questions.explanation: Substituting K equals one half m v squared into sqrt of 2 m K gives m v, so the two forms agree for nonrelativistic particles.
questions.hint: Substitute K in terms of v.

questions.topic: Momentum of a particle from its de Broglie wavelength
questions.learningObjective: Compute momentum from wavelength in pm
questions.stem: Explain how to find momentum of a particle given its de Broglie wavelength of 2.0 pm.

answer.exemplar: Use p equals h over lambda. Convert 2.0 pm to 2.0e-12 m, then p equals 6.626e-34 divided by 2.0e-12, about 3.31e-22 kg m/s. The inverse relation between wavelength and momentum gives a large momentum for a short wavelength.

questions.explanation: p equals h over lambda. With lambda equals 2.0e-12 m, p is about 3.31e-22 kg m/s.
questions.hint: Use p equals h over lambda.

questions.topic: Why an electron microscope resolves more than a light microscope
questions.stem: If electron wavelength is 0.01 nm and light wavelength is 500 nm, find the resolution improvement factor.
questions.explanation: Improvement factor equals 500 divided by 0.01 equals 50000. Electron microscopy can resolve features about 50000 times smaller.
questions.hint: Divide light wavelength by electron wavelength.

questions.topic: De Broglie wavelength at a higher accelerating voltage
questions.stem: An electron wavelength is 0.20 nm at voltage V; find wavelength in nm when voltage is 4V.
questions.explanation: Wavelength scales as 1 over sqrt of V. Quadrupling V halves the wavelength, from 0.20 nm to 0.10 nm.
questions.hint: Wavelength scales as 1 over sqrt V.

questions.topic: De Broglie wavelength of a macroscopic object
questions.stem: Why are de Broglie wavelengths of macroscopic objects never observed?

options.text: Macroscopic objects are not made of particles.
They are astronomically small, far below measurable scales.
Planck's constant is zero for large objects.
Macroscopic objects move too slowly to have waves.

questions.explanation: For macroscopic mass and speed, lambda equals h over m v is around 1e-34 m or smaller, far below any measurable length.
questions.hint: Estimate the magnitude of lambda.

questions.topic: Why neutrons diffract from crystal planes
questions.learningObjective: Explain why neutrons are useful probes
questions.stem: Why are thermal neutrons good for probing crystal structure?

options.text: They are heavier than electrons, so they travel straighter.
They have no charge, so they cannot interact at all.
Their wavelength matches interatomic spacing and they interact with nuclei.
Their wavelength is much longer than atoms.

questions.explanation: Thermal neutron wavelengths are comparable to lattice spacings, and neutrons interact with nuclei, making them excellent for crystallography.
questions.hint: Match wavelength and interaction.

questions.topic: Energy of the third energy level of hydrogen
questions.stem: A table lists E1 equals -13.6 eV and E3 equals -1.51 eV; what is the spacing?

options.text: About 13.6 eV, using E1 magnitude.
About -15.11 eV, adding the energies.
About 1.51 eV, using E3 alone.
About 12.09 eV, the difference E3 minus E1.

questions.explanation: Spacing equals E3 minus E1 equals -1.51 minus -13.6, about 12.09 eV. Energy differences are positive magnitudes.
questions.hint: Subtract the two level energies.

questions.topic: Energy needed to excite hydrogen from the ground state to n equal to 3
questions.stem: A note converts 12.09 eV to joules by multiplying by 1.602e-19; check the result.

options.text: Wrong, it should divide by 1.602e-19.
Correct, 12.09 eV equals about 1.94e-18 J.
Wrong, it should multiply by Planck's constant.
Wrong, eV cannot be converted to joules.

questions.explanation: 1 eV equals 1.602e-19 J, so 12.09 eV equals about 1.94e-18 J. Multiplying is correct.
questions.hint: 1 eV equals 1.602e-19 J.

questions.topic: Wavelength emitted in the drop from n equal to 2 to n equal to 1
questions.stem: Explain how to find the photon energy emitted when hydrogen drops from n equals 2 to n equals 1.

answer.exemplar: Subtract the final level energy from the initial level energy. E2 is -3.40 eV and E1 is -13.6 eV, so delta E equals 10.2 eV. The emitted photon carries this energy, corresponding to 121.6 nm in the ultraviolet.

questions.explanation: Photon energy equals the level spacing. E2 minus E1 equals 10.2 eV, emitted as a UV photon.
questions.hint: Subtract level energies.

questions.topic: De Broglie wavelength of a slow neutron
questions.stem: Find the kinetic energy in eV of a neutron with de Broglie wavelength 0.20 nm.
questions.explanation: K equals h squared over 2 m lambda squared. With lambda equals 0.20e-9 m and neutron mass, K is about 0.0207 eV.
questions.hint: Use K equals h squared over 2 m lambda squared.

questions.topic: The two usable forms of the de Broglie relation
questions.learningObjective: Select form based on available data
questions.stem: Given v equals 1.0e7 m/s for an electron, compute wavelength in nm using lambda equals h over m v.
questions.explanation: lambda equals 6.626e-34 divided by (9.11e-31 times 1.0e7), about 7.27e-11 m or 0.0727 nm.
questions.hint: Use electron mass and given speed.

questions.topic: Momentum of a particle from its de Broglie wavelength
questions.learningObjective: Compute momentum from wavelength in nm
questions.stem: A particle has wavelength 0.50 nm; what is its momentum?

options.text: About 3.31e-24 kg m/s, using 0.2 nm instead.
About 1.33e-27 kg m/s, using nm without conversion.
options.misconception: uses nm without converting to meters

options.text: About 1.33e-24 kg m/s, from h over 0.50 nm.
About 6.63e-24 kg m/s, using 0.1 nm instead.

questions.explanation: p equals h over 0.50e-9 m, about 1.33e-24 kg m/s.
questions.hint: Convert nm to m first.

questions.topic: Why an electron microscope resolves more than a light microscope
questions.learningObjective: Explain resolution in terms of wavelength
questions.stem: Which factor most limits the resolution of a light microscope?

options.text: The size of the specimen.
The magnification of the eyepiece.
The brightness of the lamp.
The wavelength of visible light.

questions.explanation: Resolution is fundamentally limited by wavelength. Visible light wavelengths of about 400-700 nm set the resolution limit near 200 nm.
questions.hint: Resolution depends on wavelength.

questions.topic: De Broglie wavelength at a higher accelerating voltage
questions.learningObjective: Predict wavelength ratio at new voltage
questions.stem: A table shows wavelengths at 100 V and 400 V; what is their ratio?

options.text: About 4 to 1, using voltage ratio directly.
About 2 to 1, since 400 is 4 times 100 and sqrt 4 is 2.
About 1 to 1, because wavelength is voltage independent.
About 1 to 4, reversing the ratio.

questions.explanation: Wavelength scales as 1 over sqrt V, so the ratio lambda at 100 V to lambda at 400 V is sqrt of 4 equals 2.
questions.hint: Use inverse square root scaling.

questions.topic: De Broglie wavelength of a macroscopic object
questions.learningObjective: Compute wavelength of a person walking
questions.stem: A diagram shows a 70 kg person walking at 1 m/s; estimate wavelength in meters.

options.text: About 4.6e-35 m, using half the mass.
options.misconception: uses half the mass in momentum

options.text: About 6.6e-34 m, ignoring mass.
About 9.5e-36 m, from h over 70.
About 1.3e-33 m, doubling h.

questions.explanation: lambda equals 6.626e-34 divided by (70 times 1), about 9.47e-36 m, utterly immeasurable.
questions.hint: Use lambda equals h over m v.

questions.topic: Why neutrons diffract from crystal planes
questions.stem: A note says neutrons diffract because they are charged and interact with electrons; find the error.

options.text: Neutrons do not diffract at all.
Neutrons are charged, so the note is correct.
Neutrons diffract because they are heavy.
Neutrons are neutral; they diffract due to wavelength matching lattice spacing.

questions.explanation: Neutrons are electrically neutral. They diffract because their de Broglie wavelength matches crystal plane spacing, interacting with nuclei.
questions.hint: Neutrons are neutral particles.

questions.topic: Energy of the third energy level of hydrogen
questions.stem: Explain how to compute the energy of the n equals 5 level of hydrogen.

answer.exemplar: Use E n equals negative 13.6 over n squared eV. For n equals 5, E5 equals negative 13.6 over 25, about negative 0.544 eV. The level is close to zero, meaning the electron is barely bound.

questions.explanation: E5 equals negative 13.6 over 25, about -0.544 eV. Higher n means less negative, closer to ionization.
questions.hint: Square n in the denominator.

questions.topic: Energy needed to excite hydrogen from the ground state to n equal to 3
questions.learningObjective: Identify the spectral region of excitation photon
questions.stem: Excitation from n equals 1 to n equals 3 needs 12.09 eV; find wavelength in nm.
questions.explanation: lambda equals 1240 over 12.09, about 102.6 nm, in the ultraviolet.
questions.hint: Use lambda equals 1240 over E.

questions.topic: Wavelength emitted in the drop from n equal to 2 to n equal to 1
questions.stem: Find the frequency in 1e15 Hz of the photon emitted in the n equals 2 to n equals 1 transition.
questions.explanation: Photon energy is 10.2 eV. Frequency equals E over h equals 10.2 over 4.14e-15, about 2.46e15 Hz, reported as 2.47.
questions.hint: Use f equals E over h.

questions.topic: De Broglie wavelength of a slow neutron
questions.stem: A neutron has wavelength 0.18 nm; what is its speed?

options.text: About 2.19e6 m/s, using mm instead of nm.
About 2190 m/s, from h over m lambda.
About 2.19 m/s, using m instead of nm.
About 6.63e-24 m/s, inverting h and m.

questions.explanation: v equals h over m lambda equals 6.626e-34 divided by (1.675e-27 times 0.18e-9), about 2190 m/s.
questions.hint: Use v equals h over m lambda.

questions.topic: The two usable forms of the de Broglie relation
questions.stem: For an electron with v equals 2.0e6 m/s, which form gives wavelength directly?

lambda equals h over m v, using known speed.
lambda equals c over f, light form.

questions.stem: A diagram gives wavelength 0.10 nm for an electron; find momentum in kg m/s.

About 6.63e-24 kg m/s, from h over 0.10 nm.

questions.topic: Why an electron microscope resolves more than a light microscope
questions.stem: A note says electron microscopes work because electrons are brighter than light; find the error.

options.text: Brightness is the key factor, so the note is correct.
They work because electron wavelengths are much shorter than light wavelengths.
Electrons are brighter and shorter, both matter equally.
Electron microscopes work due to higher magnification only.

questions.explanation: The advantage comes from short electron wavelengths, not brightness. Magnification alone cannot overcome the wavelength resolution limit.
questions.hint: Resolution depends on wavelength.

questions.topic: De Broglie wavelength at a higher accelerating voltage
questions.stem: Explain how to find the de Broglie wavelength of an electron accelerated through 200 V.

answer.exemplar: Use lambda equals h over sqrt of 2 m e V. With V equals 200, lambda equals 6.626e-34 divided by sqrt of 2 times 9.11e-31 times 1.602e-19 times 200, about 0.087 nm. Higher voltage shortens the wavelength.

questions.explanation: Plug V equals 200 into lambda equals h over sqrt of 2 m e V. The result is about 0.087 nm.
questions.hint: Use V in joules via e V.

questions.stem: Find the de Broglie wavelength in meters of a 0.15 kg ball moving at 30 m/s.
questions.explanation: lambda equals 6.626e-34 divided by (0.15 times 30), about 1.47e-34 m.
questions.hint: Use lambda equals h over m v.

questions.topic: Why neutrons diffract from crystal planes
questions.stem: Neutrons with wavelength 0.18 nm hit planes spaced 0.20 nm apart; find first-order Bragg angle in degrees (sin theta equals lambda over 2d).
questions.explanation: sin theta equals 0.18 divided by (2 times 0.20) equals 0.45, so theta is about 26.4 degrees.
questions.hint: Use sin theta equals lambda over 2d.

About 13.6 eV, the ground state energy.

About 3.29e15 Hz, using 13.6 eV.
About 0.82e15 Hz, using 3.40 eV.
About 2.92e15 Hz, from 12.09 eV over h.

questions.topic: Wavelength emitted in the drop from n equal to 2 to n equal to 1
questions.stem: A diagram shows the n equals 2 to n equals 1 transition; what region is the emitted light?

options.text: Visible red, about 656.3 nm.
Ultraviolet, about 121.6 nm.
Infrared, about 1875 nm.

options.text: Only charge matters for diffraction.
Wavelength is irrelevant, so the note is correct.
Wavelength determines diffraction; without matching spacing, no diffraction occurs.
Only mass matters for diffraction.

questions.explanation: Diffraction occurs when wavelength is comparable to spacing. Neutron wavelength near 0.18 nm matches crystal planes, enabling diffraction.

questions.topic: The two usable forms of the de Broglie relation

questions.stem: Explain why lambda equals h over p and lambda equals h over sqrt of 2 m K are equivalent for a nonrelativistic particle.

answer.exemplar: For a nonrelativistic particle, kinetic energy K equals one half m v squared, so momentum p equals m v equals sqrt of 2 m K. Substituting into lambda equals h over p gives lambda equals h over sqrt of 2 m K. Thus both forms describe the same wavelength.

questions.explanation: The equivalence follows from K equals one half m v squared, linking momentum and kinetic energy.
questions.hint: Substitute K in terms of v.

questions.explanation: lambda equals h over sqrt of 2 m e V. With V equals 1e5, lambda is about 3.88e-12 m or 0.00388 nm.

questions.learningObjective: Predict wavelength at 400 V from 100 V value

options.text: About 0.123 nm, unchanged.
About 0.0308 nm, quartering linearly.
About 0.246 nm, doubling incorrectly.
About 0.0615 nm, halving due to sqrt 4.

options.text: Macroscopic objects do not have momentum.
They are far smaller than any measurable length scale.
Planck's constant is effectively zero for large masses.
Large objects move too slowly to diffract.

questions.topic: Why neutrons diffract from crystal planes
questions.stem: A diagram shows neutron diffraction; what do neutrons interact with in the crystal?

options.text: Photon fields.
Electron clouds.
Atomic nuclei.
Magnetic domains only.

questions.explanation: Neutrons interact with atomic nuclei via the strong force, unlike X-rays which interact with electrons. This makes neutron diffraction complementary.
questions.hint: Neutrons are neutral and interact with nuclei.

questions.topic: Energy of the third energy level of hydrogen
questions.learningObjective: Compute wavelength of n equals 3 to n equals 2 transition
questions.stem: A note computes 656.3 nm for n equals 3 to n equals 2; check.

options.text: Wrong, energy levels are equally spaced.
Wrong, it should be 121.6 nm.
Wrong, it should be 102.6 nm.
Correct, delta E equals 1.89 eV gives 656.3 nm.

questions.explanation: E3 minus E2 equals -1.51 minus -3.40 equals 1.89 eV. lambda equals 1240 over 1.89, about 656.3 nm, the Balmer alpha line.
questions.hint: Compute delta E then lambda.

questions.topic: Energy needed to excite hydrogen from the ground state to n equal to 3
questions.stem: Explain how to find the photon wavelength that excites hydrogen from ground state to n equals 3.

answer.exemplar: First compute the energy difference between n equals 3 and n equals 1: 12.09 eV. Then convert to wavelength using lambda equals 1240 over E, giving about 102.6 nm in the ultraviolet. The photon must have at least this energy.

questions.explanation: Delta E is 12.09 eV, so lambda is 1240 over 12.09, about 102.6 nm.
questions.hint: Compute delta E then convert.

questions.topic: Wavelength emitted in the drop from n equal to 2 to n equal to 1
questions.stem: Find the emitted wavelength in nm for the n equals 2 to n equals 1 transition.
questions.explanation: Delta E equals 10.2 eV. lambda equals 1240 over 10.2, about 121.6 nm.
questions.hint: Use lambda equals 1240 over delta E.
